snapshot: WHO Western Pacific Region. A mid-sized health donor with a clear regional focus: the Pacific and Southeast Asia take priority, with health aid at about 12% of Australia's aid budget.

agenda.title: Health aid in the 2026-27 budget
agenda.text: Australian health aid is about A$647.6 million in 2026-27, almost unchanged in nominal terms (A$646.6 million the year before) and a real-terms fall of about 4.85%, according to ACFID's analysis. Contributions to global health programmes, which cover Gavi, the Global Fund and UN health agencies, rise to A$181.5 million. Regional health security falls from A$156.6 million to A$130 million, and core funding for UNAIDS and the Pandemic Fund ends after 2026-27.

agenda.title: Pacific rheumatic heart disease partnership
agenda.text: At a World Health Assembly side event in Geneva, Minister Butler announced A$5 million over four years to prevent and control rheumatic heart disease in Vanuatu and Solomon Islands, with a knowledge hub in Fiji. The money comes from the A$620 million Partnerships for a Healthy Region initiative.

agenda.title: Research partnerships in the region
agenda.text: The government is funding 24 Centres of Research Excellence through the NHMRC with A$72 million. Two have a regional or global health angle: a vaccine adjuvant centre and RESPOSTA, a One Health centre for Timor-Leste and the region, co-funded by DFAT.
